column3: “Called together” is rendered “assembled”; “officials of all the property” is rendered “overseers,” and “court-officials” as “officials.” “Every mighty man of strength” is rendered “all the valiant men.”
“I was with my heart” is rendered “I had intended,” and “a house of rest” as “a permanent home.” NASB supplies “it.”
“A man of wars” is rendered “a man of war,” and “bloods” as “blood.”
“To ruler” is rendered “to be a leader.”
NASB puts the clause about many sons in parentheses.
NASB supplies “is the one who.”
“If he will be strong to observe” is rendered “if he resolutely performs,” and “judgments” as “ordinances”; “as this day” is rendered “as is done now.”
“In the ears of” is rendered “in the hearing of”; “give as inheritance” is rendered “bequeath,” and “descendants” as “sons.”
“Complete heart” is rendered “whole heart,” and “a willing being” as “a willing mind.” “He will let himself be found by you” is rendered “He will let you find Him.”
“See” is rendered “Consider,” and “be strong” as “be courageous.”
“Pattern” is rendered “plan,” and NASB supplies “of the temple.” “Houses” is rendered “buildings,” and “the house of the atonement cover” as “the room for the mercy seat.”
“All that was in the spirit with him” is rendered “all that he had in mind”; the meaning is uncertain, as the Hebrew word can mean spirit or mind. “Holy things” is rendered “dedicated things.”
“Articles” is rendered “utensils.”
The Hebrew is terse; NASB supplies “utensils,” and “service and service” is rendered “every kind of service.”
“Lampstand and lampstand” is rendered “each lampstand”; NASB supplies “the weight of gold” and “the weight of silver.”
“Tables of the row” is rendered “tables of showbread,” and “a table and a table” as “each table.”
“Bowls” (the first word) is rendered “basins,” and “a bowl and a bowl” as “each bowl.”
“Purified” is rendered “refined”; NASB supplies “their wings.” The Hebrew phrase “the pattern of the chariot, the cherubim” is rendered with “even.”
NASB supplies “said David” and “this”; “he made clear” is rendered “made me understand.” The Hebrew is difficult, and the meaning is uncertain.
“Be brave” is rendered “courageous,” and “abandon” as “fail.”
“There!” is rendered “behold.” “Are to all your words” is rendered “will be entirely at your command.”
